Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”, a press summary handed out to reporters said. The defendants each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date. Continue reading...

Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, were charged in September 2021 with inciting subversion and face a maximum jail term of 10 years if convicted. The activists pleaded not guilty when their trial opened in January and are expected to appear in court Friday. If convicted by three government-approved judges, they likely will be sentenced at a later date.

The event immediately became an official taboo in mainland China. Authorities deemed the legislation crucial for Hong Kong’s stability following anti-government protests in 2019. The alliance voted to disband in the same month as the pair was charged. Many other leading activists are now also jailed under the 2020 law, including the pro-democracy former media tycoon Jimmy Lai. UK Foreign Office condemns use of national security law to convict activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung

Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils marking China’s deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 have been found guilty of “incitement to subversion” in one of the most high-profile cases in Hong Kong since Beijing imposed its national security law in 2020.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”, a press summary handed out to reporters said. The defendants each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow’s trial began in January and took place over 24 days. A third defendant, the 74-year-old former lawmaker Albert Ho, pleaded guilty in January. Chow, who represented herself, told the court in May that the law itself was on trial.

Lee and Chow were leaders of the now-disbanded Hong Kong Alliance, which organised the city’s annual vigil in memory of those killed in the crackdown on pro-democracy protesters in Beijing in 1989.

In court, Lee and Chow waved to supporters from the dock where they were surrounded by correctional officers. Lee appeared solemn as the judge handed down the verdict. He made a heart shaped gesture with his hands and waved to supporters before being led out of the court.

Hong Kong and Macau were formerly the only places on Chinese soil that permitted public vigils to mourn those killed on 4 June 1989, when Chinese sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital’s Tiananmen Square.

However, public commemoration has been effectively banned since Beijing imposed a national security law on Hong Kong in 2020, after huge and sometimes violent pro-democracy protests the year before.

The Alliance’s leaders were charged in 2021 and have been imprisoned since. Ahead of the verdict, Chow wrote a message from prison, seen by the Guardian, addressed to the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham. “They are trying to rewrite Hong Kong history … they certainly want to erase some memories, or memories of some chapters in our history,” the Cambridge-educated barrister wrote.

Chow added in the letter: “Britain has a non-delegable duty to adopt a more robust stance in the face of the growing threat from a totalitarian and aggressive China.”

HONG KONG (AP) — A verdict is expected Friday in the case of two organizers of an annual Hong Kong vigil to remember the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown who are being tried under a China-imposed national security law that has stifled Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement.

Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, were charged in September 2021 with inciting subversion and face a maximum jail term of 10 years if convicted.

The activists pleaded not guilty when their trial opened in January and are expected to appear in court Friday. If convicted by three government-approved judges, they likely will be sentenced at a later date.

For three decades, the now-disbanded alliance organized the only large-scale, public commemoration in China that attracted tens of thousands annually until the event was banned in 2020 following the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic.

Observers say the activists’ prosecution and the disappearance of the vigil symbolized the loss of freedoms that Beijing promised to maintain for 50 years when the former British colony returned to Chinese rule in 1997. The government said its law enforcement actions were evidence-based and strictly in accordance with the law.

The 1989 pro-democracy protests in Beijing’s Tiananmen Square were one of the biggest challenges to the Communist Party’s rule in China. The government sent tanks into the heart of the capital city and troops opened fire on the student-led demonstrations in a bloody crackdown that killed hundreds, possibly thousands.

The event immediately became an official taboo in mainland China. But the alliance held annual vigils in Hong Kong to keep memories alive across the border until authorities banned the public remembrances during the pandemic, citing risks to public health.

payload.title: Tiananmenin muistotilaisuuksien järjestäjät syyllisiksi kumoukselliseen toimintaan yllyttämiseen
payload.summary: Hongkongilaiset aktivistit Lee Cheuk-yan ja Chow Hang-tung on todettu syyllisiksi kumoukselliseen toimintaan yllyttämiseen. Heitä uhkaa enintään kymmenen vuoden vankeusrangaistus.
payload.content:
Hongkongilaiset demokratia-aktivistit Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, ja Chow Hang-tung, 41, on todettu syyllisiksi kumoukselliseen toimintaan yllyttämiseen. Kaksikko oli järjestämässä Hongkongissa vuosittaisia muistotilaisuuksia Pekingin Tiananmenin aukion vuoden 1989 väkivaltaisen tukahduttamisen muistoksi. Ratkaisu kuuluu näkyvimpiin tapauksiin sen jälkeen, kun Peking määräsi Hongkongiin kansallisen turvallisuuden lain vuonna 2020.

## Jopa kymmenen vuoden vankeusrangaistus

Toimittajille jaetun oikeuden päätöstiivistelmän mukaan Lee ja Chow yllyttivät muita järjestämään, suunnittelemaan tai toteuttamaan laittomin keinoin tekoja, joiden tarkoituksena oli valtiovallan kumoaminen, tai osallistumaan niihin. Syyksilukeminen koski nimenomaan muiden yllyttämistä näihin tekoihin. Kumpaakin uhkaa enintään kymmenen vuoden vankeusrangaistus.

Rangaistukset on määrä ilmoittaa myöhemmin, eikä niiden pituutta ratkaistu syyllisyysratkaisun yhteydessä. Lee oli aiemmin Kiinan isänmaallisia demokraattisia liikkeitä tukeneen Hongkongin liiton puheenjohtaja ja Chow sen varapuheenjohtaja. Heitä vastaan nostettiin syytteet syyskuussa 2021 kansallisen turvallisuuden lain nojalla. Aktivistit kiistivät syyllisyytensä, kun oikeudenkäynti alkoi tammikuussa.

## Muistotilaisuudet päättyivät kiellon jälkeen

Liitto järjesti Hongkongissa vuosittain kynttilävartioita, jotta vuoden 1989 tapahtumien muisto säilyisi elossa myös Manner-Kiinan rajan toisella puolella. Tiananmenin aukion tukahduttamisesta tuli Manner-Kiinassa nopeasti virallinen tabu. Julkiset vartioinnit erottivat Hongkongin Manner-Kiinasta, jossa aihe oli virallinen tabu.

Hongkongin viranomaiset kielsivät julkiset muistotilaisuudet pandemian aikana ja perustelivat ratkaisua kansanterveysriskeillä. Muutamia viikkoja kiellon jälkeen Peking määräsi Hongkongiin kansallisen turvallisuuden lain, jota käytettiin myöhemmin Leen ja Chow’n syytteissä. Laki tuli siten voimaan pian sen jälkeen, kun vuosittainen julkinen muistaminen oli keskeytetty.

Viranomaiset ovat pitäneet lakia välttämättömänä Hongkongin vakaudelle vuoden 2019 hallituksen vastaisten protestien jälkeen. Liitto päätti hajota samassa kuussa, jolloin Lee ja Chow saivat syytteet. Lain käyttöönoton jälkeen myös kymmenet muut kansalaisyhteiskunnan ryhmät ovat lopettaneet toimintansa.

Useita johtavia demokratia-aktivisteja on vangittu vuoden 2020 lain nojalla. Heihin kuuluu demokratiaa tukenut entinen mediamoguli Jimmy Lai. Britannian ulkoministeriö tuomitsi lain käyttämisen Leen ja Chow’n tuomitsemiseen.

Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils marking China’s deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 have been found guilty of “incitement to subversion” in one of the most high-profile cases in Hong Kong since Beijing imposed its national security law in 2020.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”, a press summary handed out to reporters said. The defendants each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow’s trial began in January and took place over 24 days. A third defendant, the 74-year-old former lawmaker Albert Ho, pleaded guilty in January. Chow, who represented herself, told the court in May that the law itself was on trial.

Lee and Chow were leaders of the now-disbanded Hong Kong Alliance, which organised the city’s annual vigil in memory of those killed in the crackdown on pro-democracy protesters in Beijing in 1989.

In court, Lee and Chow waved to supporters from the dock where they were surrounded by correctional officers. Lee appeared solemn as the judge handed down the verdict. He made a heart shaped gesture with his hands and waved to supporters before being led out of the court.

Hong Kong and Macau were formerly the only places on Chinese soil that permitted public vigils to mourn those killed on 4 June 1989, when Chinese sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital’s Tiananmen Square.

However, public commemoration has been effectively banned since Beijing imposed a national security law on Hong Kong in 2020, after huge and sometimes violent pro-democracy protests the year before.

The Alliance’s leaders were charged in 2021 and have been imprisoned since. Ahead of the verdict, Chow wrote a message from prison, seen by the Guardian, addressed to the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham. “They are trying to rewrite Hong Kong history … they certainly want to erase some memories, or memories of some chapters in our history,” the Cambridge-educated barrister wrote.

Chow added in the letter: “Britain has a non-delegable duty to adopt a more robust stance in the face of the growing threat from a totalitarian and aggressive China.”

HONG KONG (AP) — A verdict is expected Friday in the case of two organizers of an annual Hong Kong vigil to remember the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown who are being tried under a China-imposed national security law that has stifled Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement.

Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, were charged in September 2021 with inciting subversion and face a maximum jail term of 10 years if convicted.

The activists pleaded not guilty when their trial opened in January and are expected to appear in court Friday. If convicted by three government-approved judges, they likely will be sentenced at a later date.

For three decades, the now-disbanded alliance organized the only large-scale, public commemoration in China that attracted tens of thousands annually until the event was banned in 2020 following the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic.

Observers say the activists’ prosecution and the disappearance of the vigil symbolized the loss of freedoms that Beijing promised to maintain for 50 years when the former British colony returned to Chinese rule in 1997. The government said its law enforcement actions were evidence-based and strictly in accordance with the law.

The 1989 pro-democracy protests in Beijing’s Tiananmen Square were one of the biggest challenges to the Communist Party’s rule in China. The government sent tanks into the heart of the capital city and troops opened fire on the student-led demonstrations in a bloody crackdown that killed hundreds, possibly thousands.

The event immediately became an official taboo in mainland China. But the alliance held annual vigils in Hong Kong to keep memories alive across the border until authorities banned the public remembrances during the pandemic, citing risks to public health.

Weeks after the ban, Beijing imposed the national security law that was later used to prosecute Lee, the alliance’s former chairperson, and Chow, a former vice chair. Authorities deemed the legislation crucial for Hong Kong’s stability following anti-government protests in 2019.

The alliance voted to disband in the same month as the pair was charged.

Many other leading activists are now also jailed under the 2020 law, including the pro-democracy former media tycoon Jimmy Lai. Dozens of other civil society groups also disbanded following its introduction.

article.content:
Hongkongilaiset demokratia-aktivistit Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, ja Chow Hang-tung, 41, on todettu syyllisiksi kumoukselliseen toimintaan yllyttämiseen. Kaksikko oli järjestämässä Hongkongissa vuosittaisia muistotilaisuuksia Pekingin Tiananmenin aukion vuoden 1989 väkivaltaisen tukahduttamisen muistoksi. Ratkaisu kuuluu näkyvimpiin tapauksiin sen jälkeen, kun Peking määräsi Hongkongiin kansallisen turvallisuuden lain vuonna 2020.

## Jopa kymmenen vuoden vankeusrangaistus

Toimittajille jaetun oikeuden päätöstiivistelmän mukaan Lee ja Chow yllyttivät muita järjestämään, suunnittelemaan tai toteuttamaan laittomin keinoin tekoja, joiden tarkoituksena oli valtiovallan kumoaminen, tai osallistumaan niihin. Syyksilukeminen koski nimenomaan muiden yllyttämistä näihin tekoihin. Kumpaakin uhkaa enintään kymmenen vuoden vankeusrangaistus.

Rangaistukset on määrä ilmoittaa myöhemmin, eikä niiden pituutta ratkaistu syyllisyysratkaisun yhteydessä. Lee oli aiemmin Kiinan isänmaallisia demokraattisia liikkeitä tukeneen Hongkongin liiton puheenjohtaja ja Chow sen varapuheenjohtaja. Heitä vastaan nostettiin syytteet syyskuussa 2021 kansallisen turvallisuuden lain nojalla. Aktivistit kiistivät syyllisyytensä, kun oikeudenkäynti alkoi tammikuussa.

## Muistotilaisuudet päättyivät kiellon jälkeen

Liitto järjesti Hongkongissa vuosittain kynttilävartioita, jotta vuoden 1989 tapahtumien muisto säilyisi elossa myös Manner-Kiinan rajan toisella puolella. Tiananmenin aukion tukahduttamisesta tuli Manner-Kiinassa nopeasti virallinen tabu. Julkiset vartioinnit erottivat Hongkongin Manner-Kiinasta, jossa aihe oli virallinen tabu.

Hongkongin viranomaiset kielsivät julkiset muistotilaisuudet pandemian aikana ja perustelivat ratkaisua kansanterveysriskeillä. Muutamia viikkoja kiellon jälkeen Peking määräsi Hongkongiin kansallisen turvallisuuden lain, jota käytettiin myöhemmin Leen ja Chow’n syytteissä. Laki tuli siten voimaan pian sen jälkeen, kun vuosittainen julkinen muistaminen oli keskeytetty.

Viranomaiset ovat pitäneet lakia välttämättömänä Hongkongin vakaudelle vuoden 2019 hallituksen vastaisten protestien jälkeen. Liitto päätti hajota samassa kuussa, jolloin Lee ja Chow saivat syytteet. Lain käyttöönoton jälkeen myös kymmenet muut kansalaisyhteiskunnan ryhmät ovat lopettaneet toimintansa.

Useita johtavia demokratia-aktivisteja on vangittu vuoden 2020 lain nojalla. Heihin kuuluu demokratiaa tukenut entinen mediamoguli Jimmy Lai. Britannian ulkoministeriö tuomitsi lain käyttämisen Leen ja Chow’n tuomitsemiseen.
